name: House with Garden
tldr: 🏡 marks a home or new property, celebrates moving in, and can signal that a couple now lives together.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🏡 literally points to a house with a garden, making it useful for mentioning a home, property, or settled living space.
contextMeanings.example: We finally have a place with a little garden 🏡

contextMeanings.meaning: In relationship talk, 🏡 can imply that two people are moving in together rather than simply celebrating their relationship.
contextMeanings.example: so we got a place together 🏡

contextMeanings.meaning: With ❤️, 🏡 celebrates a romantic partner's new home and can suggest shared domestic plans.
contextMeanings.example: moving into our new place together ❤️🏡

contextMeanings.meaning: In a colleague announcement, 🏡 identifies the news as a new home, while the sentence should make the occasion clear.
contextMeanings.example: congrats to my colleague on the new home 🏡

platformNotes.note: In iMessage, 🏡 can close a sentence about keys, a move, or a shared home. Adding 🎉 or ❤️ makes the intended relationship clearer before the emoji lands.
In an Instagram caption or comment, 🏡 works as a visual marker beside a new-home announcement. A stand-alone post can invite the moving-in interpretation, so name the occasion in the caption.

In TikTok comments, 🏡 is a compact way to react to moving, housing, or settling-down content. Short comments leave little room for nuance, so pair it with words when cohabitation could be a sensitive assumption.
In WhatsApp family chats, 🏡 often sits alongside 🎉 when someone announces a new house. The combination provides context without requiring a long celebratory message.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often recognizes 🏡 as shorthand for moving in or celebrating a domestic milestone, especially beside 🎉 or ❤️.
Gen X may take 🏡 more literally as a picture of a home, particularly when it appears by itself without explanation.
Boomers may connect the garden in 🏡 with homeownership, gardening, or a long-term move rather than a romantic implication.

warnings.title: Mistaking a relationship for a move-in
warnings.description: Sending 🏡 in a relationship announcement can imply that the couple is moving in together. Mention the relationship in words and reserve 🏡 for an actual home or move.

seoDescription: What does 🏡 mean? It marks a new home, celebrates moving in, and can suggest that a couple now lives together, especially beside 🎉 or ❤️.

longForm.overview:
Introduced in Unicode 13.0, 🏡 began as a literal picture of a small house with a garden. Before its current conversational uses, that domestic scene was the point: a home, a property, the place where someone lives. The garden makes the image feel settled and private, which helps explain why it now does more than point at an address.

In messages today, 🏡 often celebrates a new home, especially when it appears with 🎉 for a family milestone. With ❤️, it can mark a romantic partner's new house. On its own in a relationship context, it can suggest moving in together. That makes 🏡 easy to misread: the picture began as a home, but its current meaning is often about the people and the change in their living situation.

The garden is what separates 🏡 from the plainer house emoji 🏠. It adds an outdoor, lived-in detail, so 🏡 feels more like a personal home than a generic property marker. Text still matters. A sentence naming the new house, the move, or the couple is safer than leaving the emoji to carry the whole announcement.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
The emoji shows up after someone gets the keys, moves, or announces a new home. Family messages often use the straightforward 🏡🎉 stack, with a sentence naming the occasion. A close friend may receive 🎉🎈 plus a sentence instead, while a colleague's new place is usually better marked by 🎉 and clear wording. An ex's new home can be left as plain text without emojis.

🏡 also appears when people are talking about living arrangements. Beside ❤️, it can celebrate a romantic partner's new home; in a relationship announcement, it can imply that two people are moving in together. People are usually trying to express a milestone, belonging, or a change in where they live rather than simply decorate the message.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🏡 by itself to announce a relationship. In that context, it reads as “moving in together,” not “congratulations on the relationship,” and can imply a decision the couple has not made. Name the relationship first and keep the emoji for a separate line.

Also avoid using 🏡 when you only mean congratulations, because the home picture can introduce a property, garden, or moving-in detail that the sentence did not intend. For a colleague's new home, use 🎉 plus a sentence. For a family move, 🏡🎉 fits. If the occasion is your partner's new place, ❤️🏡 makes the romantic context clearer.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply in the same shape the sender chose. A family 🏡🎉 deserves direct congratulations; a close friend's 🎉🎈 can be answered with 🎉 or 🎈. When someone sends ❤️🏡, a warm comment about their new place keeps the romantic warmth without turning the message into a joke.

If 🏡 appears in a relationship announcement, check what they actually mean before leaning into cohabitation. “Are you celebrating a new place?” is clearer than joking that they are already sharing a garden. If the emoji lands on your own new-home post, thank people for the congratulations and mention the practical excitement too, such as the keys or the rooms they can finally arrange.

faqs.question: What does 🏡 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🏡 usually points to a home, a new house, or moving into a place. In a relationship context, it can also imply that two people are living together.

faqs.question: Is 🏡 flirty?
faqs.answer: It can be romantic when paired with ❤️, especially when a couple is discussing a shared home. By itself, it is more about a house or move than flirtation.

faqs.question: What does 🏡 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🏡 is often used as a compact reaction to moving, buying a home, settling down, or making a shared place. The surrounding caption determines which meaning applies.

faqs.question: Why does 🏡 mean moving in together?
faqs.answer: A house placed in a relationship announcement suggests shared domestic life. Without words, people may hear “we are moving in together” instead of simply congratulations on the relationship.

conversationExamples.message: we found a place together and i really can't wait to make it ours ❤️🏡
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a romantic update about finding a shared home. Respond with excitement about the place or ask when they are moving rather than treating the emoji as a generic house reaction.

conversationExamples.message: i finally got the keys to my new place 🏡🎉
conversationExamples.interpretation: The friend is celebrating a personal milestone. A congratulatory message, 🎉, or a question about the new place fits naturally.

conversationExamples.message: our colleague closed on their new home today 🏡 congratulations to them!
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji identifies the occasion as a new home while the sentence explains who achieved it. Keep the reply professional and congratulate the colleague directly.

conversationExamples.message: mom and dad got a new house 🏡🎉 congrats!
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is the clearest family use of 🏡🎉: a household milestone with no suggestion that a couple is moving in together. Warm congratulations and a question about the house will land well.

conversationExamples.message: saving this for my future home, complete with a tiny garden 🏡
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the emoji is literal and aspirational, pointing to a home with a garden. React to the dream rather than treating it as an immediate move or relationship announcement.
